33001.story: As of Oct 16, cash rent in Belknap County ran $29 an acre in 2024. The census value of land and buildings was $5,541 an acre in 2022, up 12.8% from 2017. That value is 4th lowest of 10 in New Hampshire, under the state median of $6,630. Just 7% of the county's farmland was rented in 2022.

33003.story: As of Oct 16, Carroll County cash rent stood at $28 an acre in 2021. The census value of land and buildings came to $5,885 an acre in 2022, up 49.8% from $3,929 in 2017, or 8.4% a year. That puts the county 5th lowest of 10 in the state, under the state median of $6,630. Only 6% of farmland here was rented in 2022.

33005.story: As of Oct 16, cash rent in Cheshire County runs $71 an acre for 2026, highest of 3 in the state against a state median of $66. The census value of land and buildings came in at $7,375 an acre in 2022, up 94.5% from $3,791 in 2017, or 14.2% a year. That puts it 5th highest of 10 against a state median of $6,630. Only 11% of farmland here was rented in 2022.

Only 10% of farmland here was rented in 2022.

33013.story: As of Oct 16, cash rent in Merrimack County runs $66 an acre for 2026, the same as the state median and 2nd lowest of 3 in New Hampshire. That 2022 figure ranks 4th highest of 10 against a state median of $6,630. Only 12% of farmland here was rented in 2022.
